distractors.reason: We don't say 'look to the triangle' to mean looking at an object. 'Look to' is used for asking for help or guidance, e.g. 'look to your teacher'.
'Look on' means to watch something without taking part. We don't use it to say you see a shape on the board.
We don't say 'look with the triangle'. 'With' does not follow 'look' in this meaning.

example_sentence: Please ___ the big triangle on the board.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes suelen traducir 'mirar' solo como 'look' y olvidan la preposición. Como 'mirar' no lleva preposición en español, dicen 'look the triangle' en vez de 'look at the triangle'.
explanation: In English, 'look' needs the preposition 'at' when you direct your eyes to an object. Think of 'at' as pointing your eyes to a target.

related_collocations.example: I like to listen to music.
I wait for the bus after school.

memory_tip: LOOK AT = point your eyes at something | LOOK FOR = search for something you cannot find
